---
title: "1.6 Summary and exercise"
---

## Summary

1. Regression studies how the **mean of Y** changes when X changes.
2. A regression line has an **intercept** ($\beta_1$) and a **slope** ($\beta_2$).
3. The regression line passes through the **mean of Y at each X**, not through every data point.
4. The distance from a point to the line is the **error** (population) or the **residual** (sample).
5. **OLS** chooses the line with the **smallest sum of squared residuals**, the bottom of the SSR curve.
6. Formulas: $\hat\beta_2 = \sum x_i y_i / \sum x_i^2$ and $\hat\beta_1 = \bar Y - \hat\beta_2 \bar X$.

## Exercise

**Problem.** Study hours (X) and exam scores (Y) for four students: (1, 50), (2, 60), (3, 65), (4, 75). Compute $\hat\beta_1$ and $\hat\beta_2$, and interpret the slope.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Show answer

$\bar X = 2.5$ and $\bar Y = 62.5$.

| $x_i$ | $y_i$ | $x_i y_i$ | $x_i^2$ |
|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| −1.5 | −12.5 | 18.75 | 2.25 |
| −0.5 | −2.5 | 1.25 | 0.25 |
| 0.5 | 2.5 | 1.25 | 0.25 |
| 1.5 | 12.5 | 18.75 | 2.25 |
| | **Sum** | **40** | **5** |

$\hat\beta_2 = 40/5 = 8$ and $\hat\beta_1 = 62.5 - 8 \times 2.5 = 42.5$, so $\hat Y = 42.5 + 8X$.

Each additional hour of study is associated with an 8-point higher average exam score.
:::
